findings.issue: Calling the Corinthian danger list 'later' introduced an unnecessary letter/event chronology that the selected passages do not establish.

findings.resolution: Applied directly to latest primary prefix; source/target IDs, source bodies and counts unchanged.

findings.issue: The opening 'both ... death to law through Christ' compressed the different means phrases: Galatians says through law I died to law; Romans explicitly says through Christ's body.
findings.before: Both connect death to law through Christ with life or fruitful service for God. Romans addresses the readers' death to law through Christ's body and service in Spirit's newness; Galatians speaks personally of dying through law and living to God. The grammatical voices and extra clauses remain distinct.
findings.after: Both connect death to law with life or fruitful service for God. Romans addresses the readers' death to law through Christ's body and service in Spirit's newness; Galatians personally says that through law he died to law and then states his crucifixion with Christ. The means, grammatical voices and extra clauses remain distinct.
findings.resolution: Applied directly to latest primary prefix; source/target IDs, source bodies and counts unchanged.

findings.fix: Clarify the exact omitted words by God and distinguish the unquoted burial rule; do not leave that phrase with an ambiguous antecedent.
findings.before: The tree-hanging curse directly corresponds to Deuteronomy's death-and-burial rule. The target says cursed by God and includes burial that day; Galatians' shorter citation omits that phrase and applies the curse to Christ buying us free. That interpretation is not represented as Christ explicitly named in Deuteronomy.
findings.after: The tree-hanging curse directly corresponds to Deuteronomy's death-and-burial rule. Deuteronomy explicitly says cursed by God and requires burial that day; Galatians' shorter citation does not include by God or the burial rule, and applies the curse to Christ buying us free. Christ is not explicitly named in the Deuteronomy target.
findings.resolution: Applied directly to the current frozen3–4primary contribution; no original text,ID,range,relationship or count changed.

findings.fix: The selected Galatians unit says sons; adoption occurs in its preceding context. Name the shared sonship relation without implying the adoption word appears in4:6.
findings.before: Both include Spirit, adoption and the Abba/Father cry. Galatians says because you are sons God sent His Son's Spirit into our hearts, crying; Romans says you received adoption's Spirit in whom we cry. The you/our/we shifts and the stated crying subject remain intact.
findings.after: Both link the Spirit with sonship and the Abba/Father cry. Galatians says because you are sons God sent His Son's Spirit into our hearts, crying; Romans says you received adoption's Spirit in whom we cry. The you/our/we shifts and the stated crying subject remain intact.
findings.resolution: Applied directly to the current frozen3–4primary contribution; no original text,ID,range,relationship or count changed.

findings.fix: Replace childbirth cry with the actual rejoicing/crying-aloud instruction to the woman who is not in labor.
findings.before: The barren/deserted woman, childbirth cry and greater number of children closely correspond to Isaiah54:1. Galatians places this written passage in its mother/covenant argument; Isaiah adds for-the-Lord-has-spoken. findings.after: The barren/deserted woman, calls to rejoice and cry aloud, and greater number of children closely correspond to Isaiah54:1. Both address the woman who is not in labor. Galatians places the written passage in its mother/covenant argument; Isaiah adds for the Lord has spoken. The quotation does not independently identify Isaiah's figure as a named biological mother in Genesis.
findings.resolution: Applied directly to the current frozen3–4primary contribution; no original text,ID,range,relationship or count changed.
